thesis_summary: The primary-aluminium deficit is physically confirmed by a 32% YTD LME stock drawdown to a multi-year low and reinforced by China's binding 45 Mt cap plus independent Western smelter losses, but the only fund-positioning read (a record net long) is eight months stale, so the market's true entry-timing risk cannot be judged until the 2026-07-21 LME COTR posts.
key_risks: The Nov-2025 record net long has persisted or grown through H1-2026's price highs; a de-escalation headline (Hormuz resolution, eased Guinea bauxite export cap, weak China Politburo signal) triggers a sharp long-liquidation shakeout unrelated to the underlying deficit
Beijing grants the pending renewable-smelter exemption to the 45 Mt cap, removing the single structural driver holding the deficit in place
China's construction/property demand (new-home floor-area sales -10.8%, Jan-May 2026) worsens further, undercutting the demand side even as supply stays constrained
Vendor 2026 deficit estimates (ING/CRU ~1.2-1.4 Mt) are unofficial and have already been revised several-fold in seven months (from ~200-600kt); no official IAI/CRU balance print exists
A repeat Yunnan dry-season curtailment (~Nov 2026) is a forward risk, not yet visible, and could compound tightness right when the buffer already has little room

key_levels.fair_value_range: 3085-3200 consolidation band (chart-based, web unverified); LME cash last USD 3,154.00/tonne, 2026-07-17

relative_view: Of the four tracked commodities, aluminium has the strongest fundamentals (physically-confirmed stock drawdown, backwardation paying to hold, net-supportive macro) versus COPPER (Avoid: surplus, contango, confirmed crowded long, tariff binary), GOLD (Hold: balanced, macro headwind, confirmed crowded long, Fed-conditional), and WHEAT (Research More: deficit but war-risk-premium-inflated price, punitive contango). Its distinguishing weakness is not the fundamentals but positioning: unlike copper and gold, aluminium's crowded-long read is unconfirmed (8 months stale) rather than current.

data_needs.series: LME Commitments of Traders Report (COTR) — investment-fund net positioning, aluminium
data_needs.why_it_caps: the only confirmed fund-positioning data point (a record net long) is from Nov-2025, over eight months stale; whether that crowded long has extended or unwound through H1-2026's price highs directly determines whether a fresh entry faces a headline-driven shakeout risk, independent of the fundamental deficit case
data_needs.cap_lifted: a current COTR print (next due 2026-07-21) confirms whether the position has unwound (supports upgrading toward Buy) or extended further (sharpens the case toward Avoid), directly resolving the single biggest gap in this dossier

data_needs.series: SHFE (Shanghai Futures Exchange) registered aluminium warehouse stock
data_needs.why_it_caps: the only SHFE stock figure available is tagged to mid-April 2026 (week 16), roughly three months stale by 2026-07-18; the China on-exchange buffer cannot be placed vs. history with the same confidence as the LME read, leaving the 'how tight is China's exchange-visible buffer' question unresolved
data_needs.cap_lifted: a current SHFE stock print would let the supply-demand module state a China exchange-side tightness verdict instead of 'not assessable', sharpening the overall balance read
